CHEM.definition_en: Mentions of chemicals and drugs in biomedical text, including systematic names, trivial names, abbreviations, formulas, identifiers, families, and coordinated mentions. Each must be normalizable to a MeSH concept or compound class. Excludes vague roles (e.g. 'enzyme', 'antipsychotics'), organisms, and macromolecules above peptide scale.

DIS.definition_en: Mentions of human diseases and disorders in text. All disease mentions are annotated and normalized to MeSH, not only those linked to CID relations. Includes diagnoses and well-defined conditions. Excludes pure symptoms, adverse effect headers, biomarkers, and non-disease phenotypes.

final_task_goal: This corpus provides a MeSH-normalized NER resource with document-level chemical–disease relations. * Document pool and source: English PubMed abstracts containing diverse chemical and disease mentions. * Purpose of NER: Annotate spans for chemicals and diseases with offsets and normalize to MeSH. Disease mentions are comprehensively annotated, not limited to CID pairs. * Entity types: Two categories—Chemical (CHEM) and Disease (DIS). * Relation layer: Document-level Chemical–Induced Disease (CID) relations in line with CTD practice, including cross-sentence assertions. * Downstream applications: Benchmark disease NER and CID extraction, support MeSH indexing, knowledge-base construction, and literature-based discovery.
